title: LumiVerse v3 — choose the visual world
question: Four directions, one per style you asked to explore (neumorphic, evolved dark, light, 3D). Each comp also tests a different headline. Keep one, combine, steer, or re-roll.

options.label: Machined Instrument
options.lineage: precision lab hardware: soft-touch anodised panels, detented knobs, engraved legends
options.thesis: The studio as a precision instrument: every control is tactile, and one coral button means go.
options.viewport: A machined slate panel fills the screen. Headline 'Ambitious AI, checked before it ships.' sits in a milled recess on the left. On the right, three detented selector keys (Moj Kolega, Bridj, Air-laser) are pressed in and out like hardware buttons, showing each flagship's real screenshot in a recessed display. The coral 'Start a Project' key is the only colour.
options.risk: Neumorphism goes soft and low-contrast fast; it has to read as machined hardware, not a 2020 Dribbble shot.

raised.raise: State is shown physically: the selected flagship key sits deeper in its recess and its legend lights coral, so selection is shape, not just colour.
Process and services read as numbered assembly steps on one strict module grid that every panel snaps to.
Every number (prices, case-study stats) sits on an engraved scale or readout, measured, never floating.

options.label: Calibration Lab
options.thesis: Generation is cheap, judgement isn't: the page is a calibration bench where every project comes with its own pass mark.
materials: the dot-grid rebuilt as a measurement field
options.viewport: A near-black field where the dot-grid shader becomes an etched measurement graticule. Headline 'Generation is cheap. Judgement isn't.' at monumental scale, with 'Judgement isn't.' in coral. Below it, a row of three calibration-certificate plates for Moj Kolega, Bridj and Air-laser, each with a real number and a PASS mark. 'Start a Project' in coral.
options.risk: Closest to today's site and to the dark-agency look; it lives or dies on the certificate system being real, not decoration.

options.label: Signed-off Proof
options.lineage: the printer's proof and the Swiss identity manual: a strict grid, one ink, sign-off marks
options.thesis: Every page is a signed-off proof: bright paper, a ruthless grid, and coral as the reviewer's ink that approves the work.
options.viewport: Bright white page on a visible 12-column grid with crop marks at the corners. Huge black grotesk headline 'AI you can sign off on.' Coral proof-ink marks (a circled word, a margin tick, initials) annotate the flagship screenshots of Moj Kolega, Bridj and Air-laser laid out like proof pages. Black 'Start a Project' button with a coral tick.
options.risk: Light editorial pages can tip into a cold, generic Swiss template; the coral sign-off marks must carry the warmth and the thesis.

options.label: Scale Model
options.lineage: the architect's presentation maquette under gallery light
options.thesis: We build Better Humans, literally: every shipped project is a white scale model, and tiny coral figures are the humans it amplifies.
materials: raking gallery light and soft shadow
options.viewport: A dark gallery space with a raking spotlight on a white architectural-style maquette, a landscape of three models (Moj Kolega, Bridj, Air-laser) with tiny coral human scale figures. Headline 'We build Better Humans.' large in the upper left. A label beside each model names the project. 'Start a Project' in coral.
options.risk: Heaviest to build and load (WebGL, models); it needs strong fallbacks and can bury the work under spectacle.

options.label: Oscilloscope Bench
options.lineage: CRT oscilloscope on a signal bench
options.thesis: Projects as signals locked on a phosphor graticule.
options.viewport: A green trace sweeping a ten-division screen.
options.case: Close to the Calibration Lab but colder and more retro; high-end clients won't see themselves in a test bench.
options.risk: Retro-tech novelty, and phosphor green fights the coral.
options.kept: Every number measured against a scale, given to the Machined Instrument.

options.label: Brick Instructions
options.thesis: The studio's process as numbered exploded steps.
options.case: Too playful for high-end buyers, but its numbered-step discipline is strong.
options.kept: A strict module grid and numbered steps, given to the Machined Instrument.

options.label: Kinetic Sand Glyphs
options.thesis: Navigation by rotating rings of raised glyphs.
options.viewport: A glyph ring raised out of black sand.
options.case: Beautiful but foreign to the product; it hides the offer behind ritual.
options.risk: Unclear offer, and a palette that drops the coral.
options.kept: Selection shown as physical relief, given to the Machined Instrument.

options.label: Shell-ground Woodblock
options.thesis: Each section printed as its own colour block.
options.viewport: A centred printed subject on a shimmering ground.
options.case: No link to an AI studio's buyers; folk-craft register.
options.risk: Reads as craft, not high-impact tech.
options.kept: Build in registration order: available to the light lane's reveal.

options.label: ANSI Nightboard
options.thesis: The studio as a textmode bulletin board.
options.case: Nostalgic novelty; fails the too-playful test.
options.kept: Streamed line-by-line arrival as a possible loading moment.

options.label: Coiled Earth Tower
options.viewport: A tower of coils rising past the fold.
options.case: Earthy craft register; product clarity is weak.
options.risk: Wrong register for an AI studio.
options.kept: Projects stacked as an ascending record over time, available to the 3D lane's timeline.

canonCard.label: The premium-agency standard
canonCard.thesis: What top digital studios ship: showreel hero, giant type, a big case grid, executed impeccably.
canonCard.viewport: A full-bleed autoplay reel behind 'We build Better Humans.', then large case tiles.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from the competition by design.
